questiontext.text:
Consider two datasets, Dataset A and Dataset B which both contain two numerical variables: x and y. The summary statistics for both datasets are provided:

  • Dataset A:
    • Mean of x: 54.26
    • Mean of y: 47.83
    • Standard Deviation of x: 16.77
    • Standard Deviation of y: 26.94
    • Correlation coefficient: 0.816
  • Dataset B:
    • Mean of x: 54.26
    • Mean of y: 47.83
    • Standard Deviation of x: 16.77
    • Standard Deviation of y: 26.94
    • Correlation coefficient: 0.816

Based on the provided summary statistics, which of the following statements are true? Choose the options that you believe represent the relationship between Dataset A and Dataset B based on their summary statistics.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

questionvariables.text: ta: random_permutation([[1, false, "Both data sets will look more-or-less the same when graphically plotted."], [2, false, "Dataset A and dataset B are the same data set."], [3, false, "Dataset A and dataset B have identical scatter plots when plotting A against B."], [4, true, "The variance is larger for y than x in both data sets."], [5, false, "A scatter plot between A and B will show a strong linear relationship for both data sets."]]);

questionnote.text: Option order: {#map(lambda([i], i[1]), ta)#}. Correct options: {#[4]#}.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

feedbackvariables.text: /* opt[i] is 1 if option i has been selected, else 0, for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. We use opt[i] to give feedback in Node i + 1. */ opt: map(lambda([i], if member(i, ans1) then 1 else 0), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);

node.description: Choice 1 (Both data sets will look more-or-less the same when graphically plotted.) selected?

truefeedback.text: You selected "Both data sets will look more-or-less the same when graphically plotted.", which is not quite correct. Even though the summary statistics are the same, the datasets can have vastly different shapes and patterns. Always visualize the data to understand the true relationship.

node.description: Choice 2 (Dataset X and Dataset Y are the same data set.) selected?

truefeedback.text: You selected "Dataset X and Dataset Y are the same data set.", which is not quite correct. The datasets are different, but their summary statistics happen to be identical. This highlights the importance of not relying solely on summary statistics for drawing conclusions about the underlying data.

node.description: Choice 3 ( Dataset X and Dataset Y have identical scatter plots when plotting A against B.) selected?

truefeedback.text: You selected " Dataset X and Dataset Y have identical scatter plots when plotting A against B.", which is not quite correct. Datasets with the same summary statistics can exhibit different patterns. Visual inspection is crucial for understanding the data.

node.description: Choice 4 (The variance is larger for y than x in both data sets.) selected?

truefeedback.text: You selected "The variance is larger for y than x in both data sets.", which is correct! Since the standard deviation is larger for y than for x in both data sets, then the variance will be too. This is because the variance is the standard deviation squared.

node.description: Choice 5 (A scatter plot between A and B will show a strong linear relationship for both data sets.) selected?

truefeedback.text: You selected "A scatter plot between A and B will show a strong linear relationship for both data sets.", which is not quite correct. While the correlation coefficient is the same for both datasets, the datasets can have different shapes even with similar correlation coefficients. Visualizing the data is essential for a comprehensive understanding.
